newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Wednesday on a technical correction after successive losses in the past few days but the short-term market trend is not optimistic, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,060 yuan ($368) per tonne, rising 35 yuan. It opened at 3,000 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 2,985 and a high of 3,070.
March rose 40 to 3,035, May fell one to 3,090, July 70 to 3,100 and September 95 to 3,169. November rose 30 to 3,330.
Combined volume rose to 12,700 tonnes from 10,700.
Traders said successive falls in the past few days triggered short-covering in some contracts today but that the market trend for the short term was not optimistic.
"The contracts have been oversold according to the technical charts," said one trader. "This was the major factor today."
"Many investors were not willing to take physical goods, which is likely to cause strong selling pressure in the January contract in the next few days," he added.
Analysts expect soybean futures to fall again after the technical rebound ends. (1=8.2980)
